Đã đối chiếu (kit mục 2.11): USDA Forest Service (https://fs.usda.gov/Internet/FSE_DOCUMENTS/stelprd3817419.pdf); RSC (https://edu.rsc.org/everyday-chemistry/the-chemistry-behind-leaves-changing-colour-and-falling-from-trees/4018155.article); Britannica (https://britannica.com/story/why-do-leaves-fall-in-autumn); câu cây bàng Hà Nội lá đỏ vào mùa đông: VietNamNet (https://vietnamnet.vn/ngam-ha-noi-dep-nhu-tranh-trong-mua-la-bang-do-ruc-214928.html).
sources.text:
Why Do Leaves Change Colour?

In many countries, green leaves turn yellow, orange or red in autumn, and then they fall. Why does this happen?

A leaf is green because it has a green material called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll helps the tree to make food from sunlight, air and water. In spring and summer, the tree makes a lot of chlorophyll, so the green colour covers the other colours in the leaf.

In autumn, the days get shorter and the nights get longer. With less sunlight, the tree stops making new chlorophyll. The old chlorophyll slowly breaks down, and the green colour disappears. Now we can see yellow and orange. These colours were in the leaf all summer, but the green colour hid them.

Some trees, like maples, also make a new red colour in autumn. Their leaves are brightest after sunny days and cool nights.

Next, a thin wall grows where the leaf joins the branch, and the leaf falls. Thin leaves full of water could freeze in a cold winter, so the tree drops them.

In Hanoi, the big leaves of the Indian almond tree (cây bàng) turn red in winter. I think these red leaves are the most beautiful thing in our city.

Chưa kiểm được: "âm thanh quá cao để người nghe thấy" và "thời gian tiếng vang cho biết khoảng cách" (trang NPS về dơi chưa mở được); phụ huynh kiểm trước 17/10.
sources.text:
How Do Bats Find Food in the Dark?

Hello! Today's question is: how can a bat catch insects at night, when it is too dark to see well?

Many bats use sound. While a bat is flying, it makes very high sounds. Most of these sounds are too high for people to hear. When a sound hits an insect, it bounces back to the bat. This returning sound is called an echo.

The bat listens to the echo carefully. The echo tells the bat where the insect is. The bat also notices how long the echo takes to come back. This tells it how far away the insect is. Then the bat flies quickly and catches its dinner.

Finding things with echoes like this is called echolocation. But not all bats do it. Some big fruit bats find their food mainly with their eyes and their good sense of smell.

So next time you see a bat at night, remember: it is listening to the dark!

items.stem: In October, Nam finds a leaf that is half green and half yellow. Did the yellow colour come into the leaf in October? Explain, using the text.
items.answer: No. The yellow was in the leaf all summer; the green chlorophyll is breaking down, so now the yellow shows.

items.answer: Covered them so we could not see them (che, giấu).
items.explanation_vi: CHẨN ĐOÁN (nghĩa từ theo ngữ cảnh).

items.stem: Look at these two sentences. (A) In autumn, the days get shorter and the nights get longer. (B) I think these red leaves are the most beautiful thing in our city. Which one is an opinion? How do you know?
items.answer: (B). It says what the writer feels ('I think', 'the most beautiful') and nobody can check it. (A) can be checked, so it is a fact.
